title: Generation of hypoxia-sensing chimeric antigen receptor T cells
protocol: Identify the locus on the vector to be modified.
Synthesize a fragment containing the HRE repeats.
Double digest the SFG vector and the HRE fragment using restriction endonucleases.
Recover DNA from the gel using a DNA ladder to guide band identification.
Ligate the SFG backbone with the HRE fragment.
Identify the locus in the SFG 3′ LTR enhancer region to be replaced for a hypoxia-responsive promoter.
Synthesize the HRE fragment with the desired number of tandem HRE repeats as a synthetic DNA fragment.
Ensure the 9xHRE fragment sequence is correct (sequence details available separately).
Add XhoI and EcoRI restriction sites flanked by at least 6 b.p. overhangs to allow efficient cleavage.
Choose extra base pairs so that palindromes and primer dimers are not formed.
Digest your construct containing the SFG backbone and your synthetic DNA fragment using double restriction endonucleases in separate tubes.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 1 h.
Add Gel Loading Dye, Purple (6×) to the digestion products; 10 μL for a standard 50 μL reaction.
Run the digested sample containing loading dye on a 1% agarose gel with 0.5 μg/mL ethidium bromide until clear separation of the bands is observed.
Cut the individual bands of interest from your gel using a scalpel on a UV light box.
Minimize exposure to UV light during imaging to avoid DNA damage.
Recover the DNA from the excised gel bands using QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Ligate the digested SFG backbone and the digested HRE synthetic DNA fragment together using T4 DNA Ligase, at a molar ratio of 3:1 insert to vector.
Transform One Shot™ Stbl3™ chemically competent E. coli with the ligation mix.
Spread transformed bacteria on an LB agar plate containing 100 µg/mL ampicillin for selection.
Perform a parallel control ligation using nuclease-free water in place of the insert and transform as described above.
Grow selected colonies in 3 mL cultures of LB media containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin at 37°C with agitation for 16 hours.
Purify plasmid using a Mini Prep kit (Qiagen).
Analyze purified vectors by sequencing to confirm correct plasmid generation.
Name the confirmed plasmid as SFG-HRE.
Fuse human ODD (a.a. residues 401–603) from HIF-1α to the C-terminus of the CAR CD3ζ cytoplasmic domain.
Clone the modified CAR into the SFG-HRE construct to create a stringent dual hypoxia-dependent CAR expression system.
Identify locus on the vector SFG-HRE to be modified along with proximal unique restriction sites (NcoI/XhoI).

Synthesize fragment containing the ODD flanked by sequence identical to the CAR sequence including the proximal restriction sites identified (NcoI/XhoI) and at least 6 additional random base pairs overhangs on either side.
Double digest the SFG-HRE CAR and the ODD-containing synthetic fragment.
Recover DNA fragments from gel.
Ligate DNA fragments A and B.
Append three human HIF1α-derived ODD residues (a.a. 401–603, 530–603, and 530–653) to the luciferase gene in the reporter SFG vector.
Transduce T-47D cells with the modified SFG vector.
Expose transduced cells for 18 hours under normoxia conditions.
Assess luciferase activity in cells after exposure using a luminometer.
Stably transduce human T cells with a SFG vector containing either T4-CAR or T4-CAR-ODD (a.a. residues 401–603).
Expose the transduced T cells for 18 hours under hypoxic conditions or normoxia.
Assess surface CAR expression on T cells using flow cytometry analyses.
Normalize CAR expressing cell percentages relative to non-ODD appended CAR under normoxic conditions.
Quantify transduction efficiency of each construct by qPCR for accurate comparisons across constructs.
Synthesize the ODD fragment to be appended to the C-terminus of the CAR as a synthetic DNA fragment.
Digest your HRE-modified SFG vector with NcoI and XhoI enzymes.
Digest your synthetic DNA fragment containing the CAR-ODD using NcoI and XhoI enzymes.
Incubate the digestion reactions at 37°C for 1 hour.
Purify the digested SFG-HRE backbone (6,391 b.p.).
Purify the digested ODD synthetic DNA fragment to be used as the insert (1,824 b.p.).
Ligate the purified SFG-HRE vector and the purified CAR-ODD insert.
Transform the ligation product into competent cells.
Select transformed colonies for further analysis.
Sequence the selected clones to confirm the construct.
Validate the resulting construct containing the dual hypoxia-sensing system (HRE promoter and ODD) referred to as ‘HypoxiCAR’.
Thaw a vial of HEK293T cells in the water bath at 37°C.
Seed the content of the HEK293T vial (approximately 1 × 10^7 cells in 1 mL) in a T75 flask in 25 mL pre-warmed I10 medium.
Place the flask into an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Prepare a suspension of HEK293T cells at 2.3 × 10^5 cells/mL in I10.
Add 11 mL of the HEK293T suspension to a 100 mm plate, for a total of 2.5 × 10^6 cells per plate.
Gently rock the plate to ensure an even distribution of cells across the plate.
Place the plate into the incubator.
In a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, add 1.133 mL of IMDM media and 68 μL of FuGENE reagent.
Mix 5.6 μg RDF (RD114-encoding) envelope plasmid, 8.5 μg Peq-Pam-env, and 8.5 μg vector plasmid of interest in another 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Combine the contents of both tubes.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 15 min.
Add the mixture dropwise to the HEK293T cell plate.
Gently rock the plate to evenly distribute the mixture.
Place the plate back into the incubator.
Remove and discard media from the plate twenty four hours after transfection.
Replace with 11 mL of prewarmed fresh I10 media.
Place plate back into the incubator gently without detaching the transfected 293T cell monolayer.
Harvest the media containing viral particles forty eight hours post-transfection into a 50 mL Falcon tube and store at 4°C.
Replace with 11 mL of warm fresh I10 media.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Harvest the virus-containing media seventy two hours post-transfection into a 50 mL Falcon tube and store at 4°C.
Filter the harvested forty eight hour and seventy two hour media using a 0.45 μm sterile filter.
Use the filtered viral supernatants for T cell transduction or snap-freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C until required.
Withdraw peripheral blood from a healthy donor with informed consent.
Transfer the blood from the collection tubes to 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Dilute the blood 1:1 with RPMI media in 50 mL Falcon tubes or another sterile vessel.
Add 15 mL of Ficoll-Paque Plus to a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Transfer 30 mL of diluted blood into the Ficoll-Paque tube carefully without disturbing the Ficoll layer.
Centrifuge at 750 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C with acceleration and brake set to 0.
Transfer the PBMC layer, visible as an interface between plasma and Ficoll, using a sterile Pasteur pipette into a fresh 50 mL tube.
Remove the plasma layer above the PBMC fraction carefully using a Pasteur pipette.
Add RPMI media to reach a final volume of 50 mL in the tube containing PBMCs.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant, leaving the pelleted cells.
If more than one tube was used due to high volumes, resuspend pellets in RPMI media, combine them, and bring the final volume up to 50 mL of RPMI for a second wash.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes again.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant after the second centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of R5 media.
Count the cells from the PBMC fraction.
Proceed according to the manufacturer’s protocol for human pan T cell isolation kit.
Purify T cells using a MidiMACs separator and LS columns.
Wash CD3/CD28 Human T-Activator Dynabeads according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Resuspend purified T cells at a concentration of 3 × 10^6 cells/mL in R5 media.
Add Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28 at a bead-to-cell ratio of 1:1.
Seed 3 mL of T cells containing the Dynabeads (3 × 10^6 cells/mL) per well on a TC-treated 6-well plate.
Place the plate into an incubator.
After 24 hours, add recombinant human IL-2 at a final concentration of 100 IU/mL.
Add 20 μg/mL RetroNectin to sterile PBS with a volume corresponding to 4 μg/cm² for a non-tissue culture treated 6-well plate (2 mL of RetroNectin in PBS per well).
Place lid on the plate and wrap edges with parafilm to prevent evaporation.
Incubate the coated plate at 4°C for 16 hours.
Optional: Block plates using serum-containing media for 30 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove media after blocking and add 2 mL of virus from previous steps.
Incubate the plate with added virus for 4 h at 4°C.
Harvest cells into a tube, place on magnet for 2 min to separate beads.
Transfer supernatant containing cells to a new tube and count cells.
Add 3 mL of fresh or snap-frozen virus and 1 × 10^6 T cells in 1 mL R5 media per well.
Place plate into incubator after transduction.
Assess T cell growth every day after transduction.
On the day after T cell transduction, add recombinant human IL-2 at a final concentration of 100 IU/mL to wells.
Three days after T cell transduction, gently harvest T cells and re-plate in a 6-well plate with fresh R5 supplemented with IL-2 (100 IU/mL).
Place plate/flask into incubator.
Add R5 media and move cells into larger plates or flasks if required.
Add 100 IU/mL of IL-2 into the cultures.
Count T cells every 2–3 days and adjust their concentration to 1 × 10^6 cells/mL using fresh IL-2-supplemented R5.
Extract genomic DNA from the T cell culture using a DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (QIAGEN).
Thaw primers and KiCqStart SYBR Green qPCR ReadyMix with ROX Reagent.
Set up qPCR Master Mix as shown in ‘Materials and equipment’ section, excluding sample template.
Vortex gently to mix reaction.
Add qPCR Master Mix to the reaction plate.
Add genomic DNA to the reaction plate.
Optional: In additional wells, add nuclease-free water in place of genomic DNA for negative control.
Seal reaction plate using an adhesive PCR Plate seal.
Vortex gently to mix reaction.
Centrifuge plate at 500 × g for 1 min.
Place plate in an ABI 7900HT Fast Real Time PCR instrument.
Set real time-PCR cycling conditions according to the protocol specifications.
Collect data from the machine.
Use the threshold cycle (Ct) value of each sample for analysis.
Calculate the Ct value representing the cycle at which qPCR product reaches the set threshold value.
Assume equal transduction across the cell population for normalization purposes.
Harvest T cells from transduced and non-transduced cultures into 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend T cells in 1 mL of R5 media.
Count the cells according to your own method.
Adjust the concentration of the cell suspension to 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add 1 mL of the cell suspension to a 24-well plate for transduced constructs and non-transduced cells.
Repeat this process in another 24-well plate for both normoxia and experimental hypoxia conditions.
Place one plate inside a hypoxic chamber on top of the polycarbonate tray.
Place a Petri dish containing sterile water under the polycarbonate tray to prevent excessive evaporation.
Close the lid on the base and properly close the chamber using the ring clamp.
Attach the system to the gas flow meter and gas cylinder.
Open both clamps for the inlet and outlet tubing of the hypoxic chamber.
Connect the bottom connection of the flow meter to the inlet tubing of the tank.
Connect the tubing coming out from the flow meter to the tube inlet of the chamber.
Open the gas cylinder valve.
Adjust the regulator valve clockwise to 8–10 psi.
Set the flow meter to 25 L/min.
Purge the chamber with a flow rate of 25 L/min for 4 min.
Close the valve on the gas cylinder to stop the gas flow.
Immediately close both clamps for the inlet and outlet tubing for the hypoxic chamber.
Disconnect the tubing from the chamber.
Turn off the valve control.
Place the chamber into the incubator.
Place a normoxic plate next to the chamber inside the incubator.
After 1 hour, re-purge the chamber by repeating steps of opening valves, purging, closing valves, and disconnecting tubing.
Place the chamber back into the incubator for at least 17 hours.
Take the hypoxic chamber out of the incubator.
Open the outlet tubing clamp.
Open the hypoxic chamber by pulling the ring clamp to release the lid.
Take 200 μL of T cell suspension from normoxic and hypoxic conditions.
Add the T cell suspensions to respective wells of a 96-well plate or Eppendorf tube for antibody staining for flow cytometry.
Spin the plate or tube at 500 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 200 μL FACs buffer (PBS, 1% FBS, 0.1% sodium azide).
Proceed with standard flow cytometry detection method for CAR expression using flow cytometry.
